summary: Read-only audit of SEED-DESIGN-TAU.md's gluing relation. Confirmed the two named defects plus a third. D1: the general criteria ARE swapped - forced equal is 'every joint colouring has c1(a)=c2(b)', forced different 'every joint colouring has c1(a)!=c2(b)'; the worker states the negations. The E/N/F table is correct (re-derived), so the swap is invisible there. D2: tau=(0,10) gives an EMPTY overlap, voiding (C1). D3: (C1) mislabels its pinned pair - the 'tips' are at distance 1, hence adjacent, hence forced DIFFERENT; the forced-equal pair is (K,C1) at distance sqrt3. Replacement: the Moser spindle minus its closing edge (7 vertices, 10 edges, one shared point, no cross edges) forces a cross-copy equality at k=3, and the spindle adds that closing edge. Criterion (K1)/(K2) proven with exact quantifiers; in the multi-point form R_a[gamma] breaks once |I|>1. Cross edges only shrink J, so soundness survives; marginal blindness: pair-separation of H concerns C_k(H), not J in C_k(H)^2, so no union pair may be discarded for it, agreeing with the graph worker's retraction. For the 1145 no elimination is certifiable: the only complete data are 34 single H-colourings, which would need 58 coincidences to be joint. What IS certified is that H cannot reduce the count.

verified_results.statement: D1 CONFIRMED: the two general criteria in section 1b are interchanged. From Poss(a,b) = {(c1(a),c2(b)) : (c1,c2) in J}, forced equal is the DIAGONAL conclusion (for all joint colourings c1(a)=c2(b)) and forced different is the DISJOINTNESS conclusion (for all, c1(a)!=c2(b)). The worker states 'forced equal iff R_a cap R_b empty for every alpha', which is the criterion for forced different.

The E/N/F table is CORRECT in all five rows (E/E equal, E/N different, E/F nothing, N/N nothing needing k>=3, F/any nothing). The swap is invisible on the E/E and E/N rows because there the product-diagonal test and the intersection test happen to agree, which is exactly why the correct table coexists with the wrong general formula.

D2 CONFIRMED: with the diamond {(0,0),(1,0),(1/2,sqrt3/2),(1/2,-sqrt3/2)} and tau=(0,10), the four candidates p-tau are (0,-10),(1,-10),(1/2,sqrt3/2-10),(1/2,-sqrt3/2-10), none in the diamond, so the overlap is EMPTY. The copies are disjoint, p0 lies in copy 1 only, Proposition 1 applies, and nothing is forced. The sentence 'no overlap beyond p0' asserts an overlap that does not exist.

D3 CONFIRMED (new): in that diamond |t+ - t-| = |(0,1)| = 1, so the two 'tips' the worker calls equal-pinned are ADJACENT and hence forced DIFFERENT in every proper colouring. The forced-equal pair there is (K,C1) at distance sqrt3. So (C1) fails twice, independently of D2.

Corrected counterexample: two copies of a unit diamond glued by identifying a degree-3 vertex k1 of copy 1 with the degree-3 vertex c2 of copy 2, with no cross edge, forces c(c1) = c(c2) at k=3. Realised with unit distances this is the Moser spindle minus its closing edge: 7 = 4+4-1 vertices, 10 = 5+5 edges, no accidental unit pair. Adding the closing edge (|c1-c2| = 1 in the spindle's geometry) turns the forced equality into a contradiction, so the spindle is not 3-colourable - the forced cross-copy pair is exactly what makes it 4-chromatic.
verified_results.grade: PROOF (abstract) + PROOF of the realisation from the spindle's edge count 11 = 10 + 1; builder not re-run

verified_results.statement: Standalone criterion: with J = {(c1,c2) in C_k(H)^2 : c1(v(p))=c2(w(p)) for p in I and c1(x)!=c2(y) for (x,y) in E_x}, (a,b) is forced equal iff every member of J has c1(a)=c2(b), and forced different iff every member has c1(a)!=c2(b); otherwise both relations are realisable. Non-vacuity (J nonempty) is a separate hypothesis whose failure makes both statements true.

Multi-point form: the worker's single R_a[gamma] is an ambiguity. In copy 1 the boundary datum constrains the vertices v(p) and in copy 2 the vertices w(p), which differ for a translate (w(p) = v(p) - tau). Two functionals P_a and Q_b are required; they coincide only when |I| = 1 with v(p0) = w(p0), which is why the error is invisible in section 1b.
verified_results.grade: PROOF; fixes an ambiguity in the worker's 2b(a)

verified_results.statement: Cross edges preserve soundness: E_x only shrinks J, so (K1)/(K2) hold verbatim; cross edges can create forcing, never destroy it. What breaks is the hand argument - the colour-permutation that makes a one-point gluing inert survives a permutation of copy 2 alone only if it fixes every boundary value pointwise AND preserves all cross inequalities, a group that is usually trivial.

Marginal blindness lemma: pair-separation of H at level k states that the coordinate projections of C_k(H) are surjective; J is a subset of the PRODUCT C_k(H)^2 cut out by boundary equations and cross inequalities, and nothing about the marginals constrains the projection of J onto (a in copy 1, b in copy 2). Hence no union pair may be discarded because each H copy is pair-separating. Independently: H induced in G_rep gives C(G_rep)|_H subset C(H), so forced in H implies forced in G_rep, and H has no forced pair at k=5, so that implication eliminates nothing.

On the 1145 candidates: no certified elimination is available from existing data. Every elimination needs an existential witness, a joint colouring (c1,c2) in J; J is cut out by 58 boundary equations and 184 cross inequalities (external counts), while the only complete colouring data are the 34 verified 5-colourings of H, which are elements of C_k(H) and not of J. A pair of witnesses would need 58 prescribed coincidences to hold exactly. So additional colourings of the UNION (or of H under each boundary datum) are necessary, not optional.
verified_results.grade: PROOF of the transfer direction; the 'witnesses are silent' part is an argument, not a proof - no witness pair is known to lie in J, which is all that is established

verified_results.statement: A cheap sound refutation test, if joint colourings are ever produced: given (c1,c2) in J, if a colour permutation pi fixes every boundary value and preserves all cross inequalities while pi(c2(b)) != c2(b), then (c1, pi o c2) in J exhibits the opposite relation, so (a,b) is neither forced equal nor forced different. Sound and per-candidate cheap; it bites only where cross constraints are sparse, since 184 inequalities typically trivialise the permutation group.

Pre-registered red flag: any joint enumeration must first report whether J is empty. If J is empty the union is not 5-colourable, i.e. a 1048-vertex 6-chromatic unit-distance graph, which must be treated as a solver artefact pending DRAT rather than a result.
No forcing is claimed, no chromatic or plane-level claim is made, and the target file was not edited. All counts 1048/58/184/1145 are the graph worker's measurements, not re-verified here.

conjectures: A translate gluing with one-point overlap and NO cross edges appears to be impossible for the diamond (every difference has norm 1 or sqrt3, so any overlapping tau is either a unit vector, making every vertex adjacent to its image, or a tips difference, which I checked creates cross edges). If that generalises, the translate channel always couples, and the worker's search for a 'clean' seed is better aimed at factors with a forced-equal pair far from the overlap.

The 1145 could in principle be reduced without full enumeration by a structural pinning certificate: a vertex a is boundary-pinned only if every colouring with a given boundary datum agrees at a, which is a universal statement needing either a complete enumeration or a proof of rigidity. No such rigidity proof exists in the record.
